text: The case concerns the applicant's criminal conviction for acts of mass disorder and violence against the police during the suppression of a demonstration at Bolotnaya Square in Moscow on 6 May 2012.
The applicant was born in 1990.
The applicant lives in San Rafael, California, the USA.
The applicant was represented by Mr D. Gaynutdinov, a lawyer practising in Sofia, Bulgaria.
The Government were represented by Mr M. Galperin, Representative of the Russian Federation to the European Court of Human Rights.
The facts of the case, as submitted by the parties, may be summarised as follows.
The background facts relating to the planning, conduct and dispersal of the demonstration at Bolotnaya Square are set out in more detail in Frumkin v. Russia (no. 74568/12, §§ 7-65, 5 January 2016).

The background facts relating to the planning, conduct and dispersal of the demonstration at Bolotnaya Square are set out in more detail in Yaroslav Belousov v. Russia (nos. 2653/13 and 60980/14, §§ 7-33, 4 October 2016).
The parties' submissions on the circumstances directly relevant to the present case are set out below.
At the time of the events of 6 May 2012, the applicant was a political activist.
section_path: II. CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The applicant had previously taken part in several public protests before 6 May 2012.
section_path: II. CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: According to the applicant, on 6 May 2012 he arrived at Kaluzhskaya Square in Moscow to take part in the 'March of Millions'.
section_path: II. CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: According to the applicant, at around 6.50 p.m. on 6 May 2012 he found himself near Malyy Kamennyy Bridge in a crowd surrounded by police officers who were beating the protestors with truncheons and arresting them.
section_path: II. CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: According to the applicant, a police officer attacked him using a truncheon on 6 May 2012.
section_path: II. CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: According to the applicant, he was outraged and scared as a result of the police officer's attack.
section_path: II. CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: According to the applicant, he tried to protect himself from the blows by extending his arms forward and distancing himself from the police.
section_path: II. CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: According to the applicant, four police officers eventually grabbed him and escorted him to a police car, which took him to a police station.
section_path: II. CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: On 19 May 2012 the investigators questioned police officer Mr G., who had been present at Bolotnaya Square at the time of the events of 6 May 2012.
section_path: II. CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: Police officer Mr G. testified on 19 May 2012 that the participants of the acts of mass disorder had thrown chunks of tarmac, stones and bottles at the police.
section_path: II. CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: Police officer Mr G. testified on 19 May 2012 that the participants of the acts of mass disorder had shouted slogans.
section_path: II. CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: Police officer Mr G. stated on 19 May 2012 that neither he nor his colleagues had sustained any injuries as a result of the actions of the participants of the acts of mass disorder.
section_path: II. CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: On 22 October 2014 police officer Mr G. was questioned again, after having familiarised himself with a video recording of the events of 6 May 2012 at Bolotnaya Square.
section_path: II. CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: Police officer Mr G. confirmed on 22 October 2014 that he was depicted in the video recording together with his colleague police officer Mr K.
section_path: II. CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: In the video recording, police officers Mr G. and Mr K. were facing a thirty-year-old man with short dark hair, dressed in a red t-shirt and hooded jacket, with an umbrella in his arms.
section_path: II. CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: Police officer Mr G. stated on 22 October 2014 that the young man in the video recording provoked the police officers with his actions and words, which Mr G. could not remember.
section_path: II. CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: In response to police officers Mr G.'s and Mr K.'s attempts to apprehend the young man, the man pushed Mr K.'s hands away and tried to escape but was hampered by the crowd.
section_path: II. CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: When police officer Mr G. approached the young man, the latter hit Mr G. on the left wrist.
section_path: II. CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The video recording depicted the young man striking police officer Mr K.'s head with the umbrella.
section_path: II. CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: Police officer Mr G. stated on 22 October 2014 that he had not seen the blow to police officer Mr K.'s head with the umbrella.
section_path: II. CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: Police officer Mr G. stated on 22 October 2014 that police officer Mr K. had not told him about the blow to his head with the umbrella.
section_path: II. CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: Police officer Mr G. tried to grab the young man's clothes to apprehend him but the latter was resisting.
section_path: II. CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The video recording showed police officers Mr G. and Mr K. apprehending the young man, with the assistance of other police officers.
section_path: II. CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: Police officer Mr G. stated on 22 October 2014 that he had felt pain when the young man had hit him on the wrist but that he had sustained no injuries.
section_path: II. CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: On 22 October 2014 the police questioned the applicant about the events of 6 May 2012.
section_path: II. CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The applicant refused to make any self-incriminating statements on 22 October 2014, invoking Article 51 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation.
section_path: II. CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: After being questioned on 22 October 2014, the applicant took part in an identification parade before police officer Mr A.K.
section_path: II. CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: Police officer Mr A.K. identified the applicant in the identification parade as a person who had taken part in acts of mass disorder on 6 May 2012 in Bolotnaya Square, resisting police officers and hitting them with his hands.
section_path: II. CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: On 22 October 2014 the applicant was arrested.
section_path: II. CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: On 26 February 2015 the Basmannyy District Court of Moscow ordered the applicant's house arrest until 6 April 2015.
section_path: II. CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: On 27 February 2015 charges were brought against the applicant under Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation (participation in acts of mass disorder accompanied by violence and destruction of property).
section_path: II. CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: On 27 February 2015 charges were brought against the applicant under Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation (use of violence against a public official).
section_path: II. CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: On 3 April 2015 charges were brought against the applicant under Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation (participation in acts of mass disorder accompanied by violence and destruction of property).
section_path: II. CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: On 3 April 2015 charges were brought against the applicant under Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation (use of violence against a public official).
section_path: II. CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The charges stated that the applicant had hit Police Officer K. at least once in the left hand.
section_path: II. CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The charges stated that the applicant had hit Police Officer G. twice in the left hand.
section_path: II. CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The charges stated that the applicant had hit Police Officer K. in the head with his umbrella at least once.
section_path: II. CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: The charges stated that the applicant's actions had caused both Police Officer K. and Police Officer G. physical pain.
section_path: II. CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: On 6 August 2015 the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow began a preliminary hearing in the criminal case against the applicant.
On 20 August 2015 the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow began the trial on the merits in the criminal case against the applicant.
On 25 August 2015 Police Officer G. was examined as a witness at the trial.

Police Officer G. testified on 25 August 2015 that during the apprehension of aggressive participants of the demonstration at Bolotnaya Square, a young man later identified as the applicant had hit him twice in the left hand.
Police Officer G. testified on 25 August 2015 that the applicant had hit Police Officer K. in the head with his umbrella.
Police Officer G. testified on 25 August 2015 that the applicant had hit Police Officer K. in the left hand.
Police Officer G. testified on 25 August 2015 that the applicant's actions caused Police Officer G. pain but that he sustained no injuries.
Police Officer K. was examined as a witness on 25 August 2015 and gave statements similar to those of Police Officer G.
On 21 October 2015 Police Officer A.K. was questioned at the trial.
Police Officer A.K. stated on 21 October 2015 that he had seen the applicant at Bolotnaya Square resisting arrest and hitting police officers with his hands and an umbrella.
On 1 December 2015 Ms N., who did not know the applicant before the events of 6 May 2012, was questioned as a defence witness at the trial.
Ms N. testified on 1 December 2015 that during the clashes between protestors and the police at Bolotnaya Square she had been knocked down at some point.
Ms N. testified on 1 December 2015 that the applicant and other persons had helped her to stand up after she had been knocked down.
Ms N. testified on 1 December 2015 that after helping her stand up, the applicant had joined a group of people within six metres from her.
Ms N. testified on 1 December 2015 that at some point the applicant had been pulled out of the crowd and arrested by the police.
Ms N. testified on 1 December 2015 that the applicant had neither acted aggressively nor resisted his arrest.
On 22 December 2015 the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found the applicant guilty as charged.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that on 6 May 2012 at 5 p.m. at the latest the applicant arrived at Bolotnaya Square in Moscow to take part in the demonstration.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that between 5 p.m. and 10 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the applicant took part in acts of mass disorder accompanied by violence against police officers and the destruction of property.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that the applicant defied lawful orders of the police and military and tried to break through the police cordon on 6 May 2012.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that unidentified participants of acts of mass disorder threw chunks of tarmac, stones, sticks and other objects at the police, which hit them.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that the applicant used violence against Police Officers K. and G. which did not endanger their life or health.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that the applicant, acting with the intention of using violence, tried to prevent police officers from arresting aggressive participants of the demonstration.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that the applicant, standing in front of Police Officers K. and G., hit Police Officer K. in his left hand at least once.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that the applicant hit Police Officer G. in his left hand at least once.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that the applicant hit Police Officer K. in the head with his umbrella.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that the applicant hit Police Officer G. at least once in the left hand, causing both Police Officers K. and G. pain.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow noted that the applicant did not deny the facts shown in the video recording but pleaded not guilty and refused to testify in accordance with Article 51 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that the applicant's guilt was established by the testimonies of victims including Police Officers K. and G. and witnesses, and other evidence.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that it had no doubts as to the reliability of the evidence against the applicant.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that the fact of mass disorder taking place at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012 could be seen from the video recording.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow described the video recording as showing a young man moving in the crowd and a group of police officers in the crowd performing their duties and apprehending aggressive participants of acts of mass disorder.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow described the video recording as showing the young man with a folded umbrella approaching police officers who were arresting Mr Lutskevich and standing still.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow described the video recording as showing police officers beginning to arrest the young man, who resisted arrest, hit one police officer in the helmet with his umbrella and in the hands, and hit another police officer at least twice in the hands.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow described the video recording as showing the police arresting the young man and taking him away.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that according to an expert opinion, the young man in the video recording was identified as the applicant.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow was critical of the testimony of defence witness Ms N., finding it rebutted by the testimony of victims and other witnesses which the court accepted as reliable.
The applicant was sentenced to two years and six months' imprisonment.

The applicant's sentence of two years and six months' imprisonment was calculated on the basis of a two-year prison term under Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation, partly concurrent with a term of one year and six months under Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
The applicant appealed against the judgment of the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow of 22 December 2015.
In his appeal, the applicant indicated that the video recording did not show him hitting Police Officers G. and K.

In his appeal, the applicant argued that the statements of Police Officer G. given in 2012, soon after the events at Bolotnaya Square, confirmed that Police Officer G. had sustained neither injuries nor pain.
In his appeal, the applicant considered that the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow had unjustifiably dismissed the testimony of defence witnesses, which made the trial unfair.
On 26 April 2016 the Moscow City Court upheld the first-instance judgment of the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow of 22 December 2015.
The applicant was released on 24 August 2017, having served his prison term.
The relevant provisions of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation can be found in Frumkin v. Russia, no. 74568/12, § 78, 5 January 2016.
